A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Context Flows, with matching authors, methods and retained experiments. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original NCF experiments on Lotka-Volterra, Glycolytic Oscillator, Gray-Scott and Simple Pendulum, including benchmark comparisons and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, including additional Sel’kov, Brusselator and Navier-Stokes experiments, alongside adaptation, interpretability and ablation analyses.

M1.justification: v3 introduces NCF-t2 with second-order Taylor expansion and proximal alternating minimization, configurable context pools and L2 weight regularization. Unlike v2’s cross-context adaptation, v3 disables Taylor expansion during adaptation. These substantially change training and adaptation procedures.

E1.justification: v3 retains SP, LV, GO and GS, adding Sel’kov Model, Brusselator and Navier-Stokes evaluations. It also expands LV adaptation to a wider parameter range on a 25-by-25 grid and evaluates physical-parameter recovery. SP was already evaluated in v2’s appendix.

E2.justification: CAVIA and CoDA-l1 remain the main external baselines, and OFA remains the SP comparator. v3 additionally compares the earlier first-order NCF against NCF-t2 and includes a dedicated CoDA-versus-NCF parameter-recovery comparison in Figure 5 and Appendix A.2. The external baseline families are unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: v2 specifies 120,000 LV training epochs and GO context dimension 1024; v3 specifies 10,000 epochs for LV NCF-t1 and GO dimension 256. Optimizers, architectures and learning-rate schedules also change. New analyses introduce MAPE and matched-architecture parameter-recovery protocols. These changes do not establish that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds context-pool and Taylor-removal ablations, runtime analysis, grid-wide adaptation, attractor-specific errors, parameter recovery and GO context clustering. It replaces the SP context-size sweep with a broader LV sweep. The three-network ablation is retained, including v2 Table 4 as v3 Table 8.

E5.justification: Beyond v2’s existing uncertainty displays, v3 introduces predictive uncertainty from candidate trajectories: Figure 6 reports means and standard deviations across 9 LV and 21 SM forecasts, with deviations magnified tenfold for display. Figure 14 explicitly identifies seed-averaged results and standard-deviation bars, without specifying the seed count or establishing increased runs for retained results.

E6.justification: v3 Table 1 adds NCF-t2 and three benchmark result sets, with NCF-t2 achieving the lowest OoD MSE on five of six tasks. The first-order LV entries change from 9.56/9.83 to 6.73/7.92, in units of 10^-5 for InD/OoD, under revised settings. CoDA’s GO InD entry changes from 0.56 × 10^-3 to 5.06 × 10^-4. SP and architecture-ablation tables retain their values.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly leaves theoretical guarantees for future work. v3 adds Proposition 3.1 and its second-order JVP proof in Appendix A.1, plus a conditional convergence theorem under KL, smoothness and boundedness assumptions. The applicability of its smooth-loss assumptions to the stated L1-regularized objective is not reconciled.

C1.justification: v2 principally claims competitive generalization on three main benchmarks. v3 claims state-of-the-art OoD performance on five of six, convergence guarantees, interpretable representations and uncertainty estimation. It also elevates the benchmark collection to an explicit core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 develops contextual self-modulation, physical-parameter identifiability and explanations involving nonlinear adaptation and spurious associations. It adds substantive limitations concerning discontinuous dynamics, initialization sensitivity and hyperparameter tuning, while revising v2’s quadratic-cost discussion around context pooling and its accuracy–cost tradeoff.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands per-method architectures, optimizer and budget tables, hardware, frameworks, solver tolerances and regularization settings. It documents dataset parameters and a common split/tensor interface, and updates implementation examples for second-order expansion and pooling. Code and dataset links already existed in v2. Conflicting SP variant and LV pool-size descriptions still limit reproducibility.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating related work, v3 explicitly positions NCF relative to CAMEL/Blanke and Lelarge’s interpretable, linearly parameterized systems and claims an extension to nonlinear settings. It adds substantial positioning around proximal optimization, uncertainty estimation and scientific foundation models, supported by new references.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and discussion are substantially rewritten around meta-learning and contextual self-modulation. Extended related work moves into the main text; methods receive separate training, adaptation, pooling and testing subsections; results separate interpolation from extrapolation; and the appendices are extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: v3 merges and expands the main benchmark tables, revises the NCF diagram and adds parameter-grid heatmaps, uncertainty plots, identification panels, runtime plots and trajectory displays. Existing SP and architecture-ablation figures are relocated, while the GS visualization is retained with a revised caption. Algorithms and page layout are also substantially reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 implements the scalability remedy deferred in v2 and supports it with accuracy/runtime ablations. Broader nonlinear adaptation tests, parameter-recovery analyses and substantially fuller experimental documentation strengthen the paper’s practical evidence. These gains outweigh added tuning complexity, although conflicting settings and the unresolved applicability of the convergence theorem to the nonsmooth objective temper the stronger claims.
